## Context

## Approach
Extract a shared per-command flag-block builder (~150 lines saved). The SDK contract surface must stay byte-identical — flag-contracts feeds contracts --full and the MCP schema; run `pnpm contracts:update` and diff to prove no drift. Cross-file clone pairs to fold into the same pass: history-compact.ts:323-352 vs history-repair.ts:174-203 (chain re-anchor), create.ts:283 vs update.ts:226, list.ts:489 vs search.ts:707 (coordinate with pm-jt3b's search split), normalize.ts:427 vs update-many.ts:788, test-all.ts:37 vs test.ts:171, extension.ts:321-334 vs types.ts:821-834. Then ratchet .jscpd.json minTokens 115 → ~90.

## Definition of done
jscpd clean at the ratcheted threshold; contracts output byte-identical; suppression/gate budgets unchanged or lower.

value.text:
GH-737 maps here (no new item). CodeFactor flagged 'Using a spread operator here creates a new array unnecessarily' at src/sdk/cli-contracts/flag-contracts.ts:113, commit 0d75347f.

The flagged construct is SUBCOMMAND_GLOBAL_FLAG_CONTRACTS, an array literal whose entire body is one spread of a mapped array:

  export const SUBCOMMAND_GLOBAL_FLAG_CONTRACTS: CliFlagContract[] = [
    ...RESERVED_EXTENSION_HOST_FLAGS.map((definition) => ({ ... })),
  ];

The map already produces a new array; wrapping it in a literal copies it again. Reduces to dropping the brackets and the spread.

Mapped here rather than filed separately for two reasons. The file is this item's subject — the same per-command repetition this item exists to remove — so the restructuring will pass through this exact declaration. And the class already has an owner in the closed pm-zt1c (GH-553/GH-584, CodeFactor unnecessary-spread findings), so a fourth point item would fragment territory the registry already consolidated.

Worth carrying into the fix: the two adjacent declarations show the same shape. GLOBAL_FLAG_CONTRACTS spreads SUBCOMMAND_GLOBAL_FLAG_CONTRACTS to append a single --version entry, which is legitimate, and the comment on GOVERNANCE_AND_CONTENT_FILTER_FLAG_CONTRACTS notes it is deliberately spread into two tables at a fixed position to preserve published contract order. Any dedupe must preserve that ordering guarantee — the published flag order is contract surface.
